items.question: Who enjoys distinguished fruit by orderly way?
premises: He enjoys distinguished fruit.
This fruit comes from abandonment.
Orderly way governs all karma continuity.
items.inference: The agent who renounces fruit and follows orderly way enjoys distinguished fruit.
uncertainties: Compound segmentation of tatphalatyāgakṛtaṃ is interpretive.
items.plain_english: He enjoys distinguished fruit, made by abandoning fruit, through this orderly way, whoever has all karma continuity.

items.question: Does limited agency cast away wrong action without ego union?
premises: Without ego union, limited agency casts away.
Even with contraction, wrong action is not thus.
Some own action is intentionally held.
items.inference: Limited agency removes wrong action only when ego union is absent.
uncertainties: Sandhi splitting of sasaṃkoco@pi and so@kalaḥ is interpretive.
items.plain_english: Without ego union, limited agency casts away; even with contraction, wrong action is not thus, nor is some own action intentionally held.

items.question: Would true speech be known to another by you?
premises: True speech would not be known to another.
The enjoyer's intention is thus.
Intention in self is the measure.
items.inference: Knowledge of true speech depends on intention matching that of the enjoyer.
uncertainties: Long compound cetsyādabhisaṃdhiryathātmani has multiple possible splits.
items.plain_english: True speech would not be known to another by you; the enjoyer's intention would be thus, as intention is in self.

items.question: Would another's wrong action necessarily exist?
premises: That wrong action would necessarily be another's.
Other intention awareness is the condition.
Own intention becomes firm thereby.
items.inference: Another's wrong action arises when awareness of other intention makes own intention firm.
uncertainties: Compound satastadduṣkṛtaṃ may be read as existing wrong action.
items.plain_english: That wrong action would necessarily be another's existing one; in awareness of other intention, own intention becomes firm.

items.question: Is there fruit connection in absence of intention?
premises: In absence of intention, this has no fruit connection.
The convention 'wrong action is mine' is not so.
That convention is for fruitlessness.
items.inference: Without intention, no fruit connection follows, and ownership convention yields no fruit.
uncertainties: rūḍhistasyāphalāya can be read as convention leading to fruitlessness.
items.plain_english: In absence of intention, this has no fruit connection; the convention 'wrong action is mine' is not so, and that convention is for fruitlessness.

items.question: Would fruit arise for both when other intention is cut?
premises: When other intention is cut, both are not intentionally held by self.
Fruit would not be for both.
Destruction cause is established.
items.inference: Cutting other intention removes fruit for both because intentional holding ceases.
uncertainties: syānnāśahetuvyavasthiteḥ is a long sandhi compound.
items.plain_english: When other intention is cut, both are not intentionally held by self; fruit would not be, due to established destruction cause.

items.question: Is enjoyment of virtue fruit just in pleasure cause?
premises: In pleasure cause and pleasure, this has common intention.
Even from undifferentiated, it is just.
Enjoyment of virtue and other fruit follows.
items.inference: Common intention makes enjoyment of virtue fruit just even in undifferentiated pleasure.
uncertainties: sāmānyādabhisaṃdhitaḥ may mean from common intention or from generality.
items.plain_english: In pleasure cause and pleasure, this has common intention; even from undifferentiated, just enjoyment of virtue and other fruit follows.

items.question: Would suffering or its cause be mine thus?
premises: Suffering or suffering cause would be mine thus.
Again, common intention is not so.
Unvirtue would not be scripture.
items.inference: Common intention does not make suffering or unvirtue one's own, and unvirtue is not scripture.
items.plain_english: Suffering or its cause would be mine thus; but again common intention is not so, and unvirtue would not be scripture.

items.question: What do we speak about the subject?
premises: We speak the subject.
It concerns knowledge-limited described course.
Without ego union, all karma impressions dissolve.
items.inference: The subject is that without ego union all karma impressions dissolve.
items.plain_english: We speak the subject: for the knowledge-limited described course, without ego union all karma impressions dissolve.

items.question: Therefore does karma exist for this?
premises: Therefore karma does not exist for this.
Impurity may do cooperation.
By that this enjoys destruction state.
items.inference: Karma does not exist for this; impurity's cooperation leads to destruction state.
uncertainties: tenāyaṃ and dhvaṃsamānatvamaśnute are compound readings.
items.plain_english: Therefore karma does not exist for this; let impurity do cooperation, by that this enjoys destruction state.

items.question: Does one with destroyed impurity and inner Shiva possession go to karma-dependent activity?
premises: Impurity is destroyed and inner Shiva possession controls.
Even ego state goes.
Karma-dependent activity is not reached.
items.inference: One whose impurity is destroyed and who is controlled by inner Shiva does not fall into karma-dependent activity.
uncertainties: apadhvastamalastvantaḥśivāveśavaśīkṛtaḥ is a very long compound.
items.plain_english: With impurity destroyed and controlled by inner Shiva possession, even ego state goes, not to karma-dependent activity.

items.question: What was said in holy previous scripture?
premises: It was said in holy previous scripture.
By supreme lord, that is this.
They desire impurity as ignorance.
Impurity is cause of world sprout.
items.inference: Holy previous scripture says supreme lord identifies impurity as ignorance and cause of world sprout.
uncertainties: malamajñānamicchanti may be read as 'they call impurity ignorance'.
items.plain_english: It was said in holy previous scripture, and by supreme lord that is this: they desire impurity as ignorance, cause of world sprout.
